keyVerseText: Ishmerai also, and Jezliah, and Jobab, the sons of Elpaal;
rootMeaning: The name יִזְלִיאָה (Yizlîyʼâh) possibly derives from an unused Hebrew root meaning "to draw up," which suggests the idea of drawing out or preserving. This etymological insight enriches the understanding of the name Jezliah as "whom God will preserve," emphasizing divine protection and sustenance rather than merely a personal identifier. The literal root sense conveys an active divine involvement in safeguarding or delivering, which goes beyond a simple proper name to imply ongoing care.
usageInScripture: The word יִזְלִיאָה appears only once in Scripture, specifically in 1 Chronicles 8:18, where it is used as a proper name for a Benjamite, a son of Elpaal. The translation consistently renders it as Jezliah, maintaining its identity as a personal name without variation. This singular occurrence highlights the name's specific genealogical role within the tribe of Benjamin, reflecting its use as a marker of lineage rather than a common noun or concept.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, the meaning of Jezliah as "whom God will preserve" underscores the biblical theme of God's providential care over His people. Even in genealogical records, names carry deep spiritual significance, reminding believers that their identity and heritage are under divine protection. This preservation theme points forward to the ultimate preservation found in Christ, who secures salvation and eternal life for His followers. Recognizing such names invites believers to trust in God's sustaining power throughout generations.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Chronicles 8:18, the verse lists Ishmerai, Jezliah, and Jobab as sons of Elpaal, situating Jezliah within the family line of Benjamin. The inclusion of Jezliah here not only preserves historical lineage but also subtly conveys God's ongoing preservation of His covenant people. The name Jezliah enriches this genealogical record with a reminder that God actively preserves the faithful, reinforcing the continuity of His promises through generations.
